newsitem.title: USA: 3M sees $800 mln Pacing Plus sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: 3M sees $800 mln Pacing Plus sales in 1997.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co expects sales from its Pacing Plus programs to reach $800 million this year, up from $400 million in 1996, said chairman and chief executive L.D. DeSimone on Tuesday.

At the company's annual meeting, DeSimone told shareholders, "Our Pacing Plus programs generated $400 million of sales in 1996. This year, we expect sales from these programs to double to about $800 million."

Products in the programs include microflex brand circuits used in ink-jet printers and other electronic products. DeSimone said 3M recently authorized $180 million for new flexible circuit production plants.

Microreplication technology, from which 3M derives products such as brightness enhancement film for laptop computers, was incorporated in products accounting for about five percent of 1996 sales, DeSimone said.
"Within five years, 25 percent of our sales, more than $5 billion, could come from products that have some microreplication content," DeSimone said.

About 53 percent of 3M's 1996 sales of $14.2 billion came from non-U.S. markets. "The economies in core European countries like Germany and France are slow and the prospects are not encouraging for the near term," DeSimone said.
"On the other hand, Central Europe, paced by Poland and the Czech Republic, continues to advance," he said.
3M expects to open a company in Romania by year's end, he added.
"In Japan, home of 3M's largest international company, we hold leading positions in all our major businesses. We continue to show double-digit unit growth, despite a sluggish economy," DeSimone said.
The company operates in a dozen other Asian countries. "Sales by these 12 companies are approaching $1 billion and continue to grow at 20-plus percent," he said.
